column1: # How each network-dependent piece of a staged nf-core pipeline is handled
# on Hazel, where compute nodes have no outbound internet. Read by
# gen_network_config.py, which renders the Nextflow config fragments that
# implement it into the site config dir (NF2OOD_SITE_CONFIG_DIR, read by
# every generated OOD app's launcher), and by json2ood.py for its form rows.
# To deploy a change:
#   ./gen_network_config.py site/hazel_network.tsv "$NF2OOD_SITE_CONFIG_DIR"
# Only hide/hint/precache changes (form rows) also need apps regenerated.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Format: <pipeline>\t<process>\t<action>\t<param>\t<value>\t<note>
#   pipeline  nf-core pipeline slug (e.g. mag), or * for every pipeline.
#             route/deny rows must use *: they are process-name rules in
#             the shared hazel_network.config, and nf-core modules keep
#             the same process name across pipelines.
#   process   process name (a Java regex, matched against the simple name),
#             or - for a param that Nextflow itself fetches from the launcher
#             job rather than a task (e.g. a remote URL default).
#   action    route    run the process on the xfer partition (outbound
#                      internet), with capped resources. For small downloads
#                      that change often, where a local mirror isn't worth it.
#             precache set <param>=<value> in pipeline/<pipeline>.json,
#                      which the launcher merges under the form's params.
#                      The pipeline skips its download when the param is set,
#                      so the process never runs.
#             deny     fail the process immediately with a message naming
#                      <param>. For downloads too large to fetch per run that
#                      haven't been pre-cached yet.
#             todo     undecided; rendered as a comment only.
#             hide     leave <param> out of the generated OOD forms. For a
#                      pipeline's own download switch whose process is
#                      denied, so OOD users can't pick an option that fails.
#                      Read by json2ood.py (via NF2OOD_NETWORK_TABLE), not
#                      gen_network_config.py; process is -.
#             process  add the Nextflow directive in <value> (e.g. an ext.args
#                      closure) to <process> in pipeline/<pipeline>.config,
#                      which the launcher passes with -c, also under the test
#                      profile. For tool flags a no-internet node needs that
#                      the pipeline doesn't set. param is -. A directive set
#                      this way replaces the pipeline's own value for it, so
#                      carry over any logic the pipeline had. Write process
#                      exactly as the pipeline's own withName selector, so
#                      the rule merges into that block.
#             hint     add "a local copy is available: <value>" to <param>'s
#                      help text in the generated OOD forms, without setting
#                      it. Also json2ood.py only; see the precache rule below.
#   param     pipeline param (precache: the one to set; deny/todo: the one a
#             user should set instead), or -.
#   value     precache/hint: the local path; - otherwise. precache also
#             takes null, to clear a remote URL default that nf-schema
#             validation checks for existence (it can't offline) when the
#             pipeline only uses it in an off-by-default mode; and true/false,
#             for a site default of a flag (the form then shows that value).
#   note      free text, copied into the generated config as a comment.
# precache vs hint: precache a param only if setting it changes *which*
# database a step uses, never *whether* the step runs. Some params are also
# the step's on-switch -- mag runs CAT whenever cat_db is set and MetaEuk
# whenever metaeuk_db is set -- so precaching one would turn that step on
# for every run (and mag errors if it's combined with the matching download
# switch). Use hint for those, so users opt in by pasting the path.
# precache rows also blank the param's pre-filled schema default in the OOD
# form, with help text naming the local copy, since a submitted value
# overrides the config.
# Process names not listed here that still look like downloads
# (*DOWNLOAD*, *UPDATE*, *DATASETGET, *DATABASES) are routed to xfer by a
# catch-all in gen_network_config.py, so a new pipeline version degrades to
# "slow on xfer" rather than "fails on compute" until it's classified here.
# --- route: small, frequently updated downloads --------------------------
